content: The World Health Organization (WHO) published guidelines in 2019 regarding the treatment of drug-resistant tuberculosis (TB). These guidelines are available for non-commercial use, provided proper citation is given. The original English version remains the authoritative edition. Disputes arising from the use of the license are subject to mediation under the rules of the World Intellectual Property Organization. The guidelines include recommendations for the treatment of drug-resistant TB, based on evidence reviewed using the GRADE methodology. These recommendations consider the quality of evidence, the balance of benefits and harms, resource implications, feasibility, and patient values and preferences. The guidelines were developed through a series of meetings involving experts in TB treatment, including clinicians, researchers, and representatives from national TB programs and civil society. Participants included specialists in clinical practice, pharmacology, epidemiology, and program management. The meetings also involved discussions on the composition and duration of treatment regimens for multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) in adults and children, as well as considerations for HIV-positive patients and those with isoniazid-resistant TB. The WHO emphasizes that the information in the guidelines has been carefully verified, but it is distributed without any warranty. The responsibility for interpreting and using the material lies with the reader, and WHO is not liable for any damages resulting from its use. The guidelines are part of WHO's commitment to transparency and evidence-based recommendations for the management of drug-resistant TB.
